column1: # Braden (2006) Fig 5.3, element 1 'LIST' (Mouthpiece & lead-pipe) of the Conn 88H template: DIGITIZED FROM A FIGURE, NOT A MEASURED TABLE.
# Source: A. C. P. Braden, Bore Optimisation and Impedance Modelling of Brass Musical Instruments, PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh, 2006,
#   Figure 5.3 'Bore-profile generated by template from table 5.1 with each element numbered', thesis p.71 (PDF page 88). The text of Table 5.1 p.72
#   prints this element only by its length 26.145 cm and its end radii 1.286 -> 0.664 cm; the interior below is read from the figure.
# Method: pdfimages -png of the page gives the native 1-bit 300 ppi scan (2369 x 3452 px). Axes calibrated from the frame ticks. The profile is the
#   centre of its 3-5 px stroke: lowest dark cluster per pixel column for the gentle parts, per pixel row for the steep cup wall (rows 925-931 skipped:
#   the y = 1 cm tick mark of the left axis crosses the wall there). Stations every 4 columns (cup wall: every 4 rows, merged when closer than 0.15 cm).
# Calibration: x: 6.430 px/cm from the five ticks 50..250 cm (tick residual up to 1.8 px); x = 0 at the left axis line centre (px 415.5; the tick fit
#   puts it at 414.7). y: 74.342 px/cm from the nine ticks 2..10 cm (residual up to 0.36 px); r = 0 at px 1001.38. The drawn end of the element (start of
#   the ramp that draws the printed 0.664 -> 0.695 jump, px 584.5) is 26.283 cm from the origin against the printed 26.145 cm: all x are multiplied by
#   S = 0.99475 so the table's printed length is exact. First and last radii are the PRINTED 1.286 and 0.664 (the stroke centre reads 1.256 at
#   0.6 cm and 0.653 at the end).
# Checks against printed values (not fit targets): the main-slide stroke (element 3) reads r = 0.691 cm against the printed 0.695; the element-end stroke
#   0.653 against 0.664; the drawn end ramp starts within 1 px (0.16 cm) of the printed element length.
# Estimated uncertainty (a judgement from the pixel size and the checks above, not a stated source uncertainty): radius +-0.015 cm (1 px = 0.0134 cm);
#   axial position +-0.3 cm (frame and tick origins differ by 0.8 px, tick residual 1.8 px, stroke thickness); the steep cup wall is most affected, so the
#   volume of the first 3.5 cm (cup and throat) is about +-1.5 ml. Features narrower than 1 px or 0.16 cm (the rim fillet, any shoulder inside the
#   first 0.6 cm) are not resolved. The two steps are drawn by the thesis as short ramps (about 1 cm and 0.8 cm wide); they are treated as radius steps
#   at the ramp centre (px 466) and at the printed element end.
# Result: 35 stations, 33 segments, length 26.1450 cm, total volume 35.4 ml, cup and throat (first 3.5 cm) 9.5 ml,
#   minimum radius 0.388 cm at 3.79 cm. The cup is INSIDE this element, so a separate lumped cup volume would count it twice.
